newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share prices tumble on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share prices tumble on profit-taking.

text.p: Share prices tumbled at Wednesday's trading on the Nigerian stock market, spurred by profit taking and adjustment of multinational conglomerate Lever Brothers for dividend payment, dealers said.
The all-share index slumped to 8729.29 from 8780.05 on Tuesday.
"Investors feel the shares have peaked and would rather convert their paper money to cash," said one dealer. "Why not sell the paper and buy, say, a car?"
Lever Brothers, which announced full year results in the week, went ex-dividend, closing 95 kobo down at 28.95 naira.
The price crash also hit the banking and petroleum products marketing sectors.
The four major banks fell as investors opted to take their profit after hefty price appreciations, dealers said.
United Bank for Africa was down 70 kobo to 13.80 naira. Union Bank shed 40 kobo to 16.30 naira and Frist Bank fell six kobo to 15.65 naira.
Among the oil marketers, Unipetrol closed 50 kobo down at 73.00 naira, Agip lost 48 kobo at 26.00 naira while Total finished 20 kobo down at 60.70 naira.
Traders said Mobil, however, rose to 61.50 naira, up 20 kobo, while Texaco was up by 25 kobo to close at 46.50 naira.

Cheering news also came from Industrial Gases which on Wednesday posted an improved half-year result, raising its net profit to end-March 1997 to 45.47 million naira from 31.19 million in the comparable period last year.
Industrial Gases rose 45 kobo to 11.80 naira.
West African Portland Cement Company WAPP which also announced lower full year profits dropped 10 kobo to 66.50.
